_note: Pre-registered 2026-11-03, BEFORE any open-price data was downloaded or any result existed. Do not edit to fit a result. To change a criterion, add a dated entry to docs/research/log.md saying why, then edit.
idea: Overnight drift: buy the close, sell the next open, every trading day. Sources: Cooper, Cliff, Gulen (2008); Lou, Polk, Skouras (2019); later persistence work (search summaries, papers not read). All sources are gross of costs, which is exactly what this test adds. See docs/research/swing-trading-research.md section 2G.
instrument_note: Fixed now. SPY is the primary; QQQ is a confirmation. No other instruments will be tried.

rule.entry: buy at the day's close (a market-on-close order in practice)
rule.exit: sell at the next trading day's open (a market-on-open order in practice)
rule.position: all of equity in whole shares; cash residual idle at 0
rule.prices: IBKR daily bars, ADJUSTED_LAST (split and dividend adjusted). Today's unfinished bar dropped. The adjusted open and close are checked for consistency on a known ex-dividend date before the run.
rule.costs: tempo.backtest.Costs commission and the SEC fee on the sell, plus slippage in bps per side
rule.capital: 100,000 primary; 10,000 reported as well (the 1.00 minimum commission matters at that size)

reported_not_criteria: intraday leg (open to close) mean daily return, to show the tug of war
buy and hold over the same days
break-even slippage per side: the bps per side at which net CAGR reaches 0
shuffle_control: Not used: shuffling days does not change a mean drift, so it cannot tell us anything here. The t-statistic and the half-sample split carry that job.
pass_all_of: SPY net Sharpe at 1 bp per side >= SPY buy-and-hold Sharpe over the same days
SPY net CAGR > 0 at 3 bps per side (a 3x margin over the 1 bp assumption)
SPY net CAGR > 0 at 1 bp per side in both halves of the sample
SPY net CAGR > 0 at 1 bp per side in the post-2010 part alone (the original studies end in 2006)
t-statistic of SPY's mean daily net return at 1 bp per side > 3.0 (Harvey, Liu, Zhu)
SPY max drawdown shallower than SPY buy and hold
QQQ passes the CAGR-at-3-bps, both-halves, and Sharpe-vs-buy-and-hold criteria too
if_fail: Report it as a failure. Report the break-even slippage anyway: it tells us how much room a better execution would need. No extra instruments, no parameter changes.
if_pass: Still not proof of an edge and not real money: next step is a fill-and-slippage log on the paper account (market-on-close and market-on-open orders through tempo/orders.py), because slippage is the one number we only assume.
